projects.title: Parallax Archive Terminal System
projects.tagline: One canonical archive expressed through six distinct terminal experiences: Discovery, Origin, Creation, Play, Gallery, and Deployment.
projects.story: The Parallax Archive Terminal System turns a conventional portfolio into an explorable place. Six machine shells share the same Archive Core project truth while translating it into different emotional and operational languages. The system begins with a physical business card, passes through a professional contact page and Archive Gateway, and opens into terminal experiences that remain directly linkable and accessible without simulation layers.
projects.summary: The Archive Terminal System is the working public infrastructure beneath the Parallax gallery. It proves the central architectural ruling: author project truth once, publish it once, and let every machine inherit it without creating six competing copies.
projects.see: The six live terminals, shared Archive Core records, stable deep links, published artifact cards, direct project routes, accessible Network fallback, and the first source-led publication pack.
projects.proof: Six interactive terminal shells are live over one shared manifest. The repository includes syntax-gated public JavaScript, direct project records, responsive fallbacks, three reviewed vector visuals, and six public briefs derived from canonical design documents.
projects.next: Apply the same publication workflow to Parallax Mendala, Graph Cinema, Carbon Loop, games, music, and field-system records while connecting full canonical source files only after public-safety and layout review.
projects.claimBoundary: This is a working public archive and presentation system, not a complete digital-preservation platform, legacy-computer emulator, or substitute for the canonical offline source library. Public briefs summarize retained DOCX sources; they do not silently replace them.
